title: P2 authored compressed raw terrain arrays, HD off
scope: Production raw terrain/water atlas loading only. HD and padded detail use their existing decoded processing paths. No setting, native-engine patch or deployment.
contract: Preserve every authored DXT mip block or decoded authored pixel; generate only the established missing tail.
Use eligible compression according to RenderingServer S3TC support. Normalize the entire array to RGBA if its layer formats differ; preserve authored levels during conversion.
Retain BC1 transparency fallback, missing/malformed dimension magenta placeholders, resource-prefix aliases, single-layer maps and HD latched at map load.
Texture sampling remains in the existing shader/filter/color-space path. The old regenerated mip chain is not the visual oracle.
Generated BC1 tails are lossy; a mixed RGBA array retains the decoded generated blocks of its otherwise compressible layers.

census.exception: LiA zonefinal layer 001 has four authored 512-square mips, so the bounded tail policy makes it RGBA. All three layers normalize to RGBA. zone3dun1 has one fully authored ten-mip DXT1 layer and remains compressed.
census.interpretation: Sum of per-map array payloads, not a deduplicated asset corpus or simultaneous whole-game residency.

scene_assessment: 32 paired complete terrain/water views use an independent authored-RGBA control. Forward+ and Compatibility bz2g peak at 3/255; authored RGBA zonefinal differs by 1/255 at three pixels in one far view because otherwise eligible layers keep their quantized generated tails.

Mobile zone1 is deterministic: the unchanged candidate replay is byte-identical in all eight views. The independent authored-RGBA control has two distant pixels up to 15/255; matching the generated BC1 tail blocks removes those, leaving at most 4/255 in that view.

Four close-view dark-blue pixels remain at 7/255 against the decoded-block control, representing the native-BC versus CPU-decode difference after the existing spatial material/color pipeline. Raw nearest-LOD sampling stays at or below 3/255; its 6/255 established allowance is not silently widened.
Padded detail without visible water is byte-identical; raw-atlas water remains subject to its documented BC sampling differences. Draw counts agree for all reference pairs.

Eight full screenshots were visually inspected: original/changed near and far green terrain, near and far LiA terrain with its decoded control, lava in the fallback map, and coastal water. No missing tiles, orientation changes or visible seams were found.

review: Independent read-only review by gameplay_camp_ui found no actionable production or lifecycle defect. It confirmed both engine upload paths submit supplied mip chains and identified selected-LOD rather than full-chain GLES sampling as an evidence limit.
limits: Linux exported runtime, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 / driver 580.178.04 only. No Android, Web, Windows, macOS or second-vendor acceptance.

OpenGL layer readback cannot establish retained authored mip levels. Vulkan exact readback covers all 588 real layers; GLES explicit LOD sampling covers selected layers/levels plus the CPU full-corpus checks.

Engine-reported allocation deltas are not total physical VRAM, peak process memory or FPS. Eight-layer zone1 raw allocation: Vulkan 11206656 -> 1441792 bytes, GLES 11184800 -> 1398208. Padded allocations are unchanged; both arrays return to the same baseline after release.

Single-load timing observations are retained, not a speedup claim. Tail encoding, transparency scans and mixed-array decoding can add loading work. In the recorded Vulkan pair, raw zonefinal loading was 1.8 -> 5.0 ms; source I/O cache and a concurrent headless ordinary gameplay route were not isolated.
The HD GPU payload remains RGBA8 and no HD memory policy was changed. Existing upscaler guards pass 501 checks. The earlier native worker-pool exit issue is not fixed by this work.
The accepted pack is an isolated abda715 game snapshot plus the exact terrain overlay hash recorded above; unrelated P1 test work is excluded. User data archives and saves are read-only.
